impact_scope.description: The existing ares_reinit lifecycle call changes internal lock timing: system configuration is retrieved before locking, while applying it to the channel is now locked inside ares__init_by_sysconfig. The public callable and its caller-supplied arguments are unchanged.

evidence: In S0, ares_reinit(ares_channel_t *channel) already exists as the anchored public lifecycle callable.
H0 only fuzzes query creation and DNS reply parsers; it never creates a channel or invokes ares_reinit.
In S1, the same ares_reinit(ares_channel_t *channel) declaration and call signature remain.
H0 remains unchanged and still does not create a channel or invoke ares_reinit; moving lock ownership within the existing call chain does not add a distinct harness entry or input obligation.

new_harness_obligation.description: No new H0 action is required relative to S0. Exercising the changed synchronization still uses the already-existing ares_reinit call and channel lifecycle; the internal lock handoff supplies no new caller argument, configuration, buffer, or call-order requirement.
evidence: The ares_reinit signature is identical in S0 and S1.
The only changes move channel locking between ares_reinit and ares__init_by_sysconfig.
H0 omitted the identical reinitialization lifecycle path on both sides.

reason: The principal unit is the existing anchored ares_reinit lifecycle path, specifically its system-configuration locking behavior. Its exposure gap is true in both snapshots because H0 never calls it. The commit changes internal synchronization without changing how the harness must reach or control the callable, so the gap is UNCHANGED and does not trigger maintenance.
